roadmap.goal: Story #6083 — switch 'Fill in past days on over-time charts' (OverTimeHistoryFill) on by default. Two production moves, each with the test rework it forces in the same commit: (1) OptionalFeatureSeeder seeds the fill on, switches an existing row on exactly once, and records that it did in AppSettings under AppSettingKeys.HistoryFillSwitchedOnByDefault (Id = 0, never in AppSettingSeeder's defaults list), on fresh installs as well as upgrades, so an administrator's later off holds across every restart; (2) a database restore never makes that switch-on — the fill comes back exactly as the backup held it and stays that way after a restart — while clearing the database behaves as a new instance. Then the user-facing docs and ARCHITECTURE.md stop describing an opt-in, and the E2E suite stops assuming the fill ships off. Done when: all ten Story6083HistoryFillOnByDefaultTest cases and the three seeder unit tests (OptionalFeatureSeederTests x2, AppSettingSeederTests x1) are un-ignored and green; `grep -rn "PendingDeliver\|pending DELIVER" Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/API/Integration/BehaviourSettings/Story6083* Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/Services/Implementation/Seeding` returns zero matches; `dotnet build` has zero warnings; the backend suite is green with `--filter "TestCategory!=Integration&TestCategory!=JiraIntegration&TestCategory!=LinearIntegration&TestCategory!=AdoIntegration&TestCategory!=ServiceNowIntegration"`; `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` are green with zero warnings. Lighthouse-Clients copy, the release-notes line, screenshot regeneration and Stryker mutation testing are separate gates the maintainer runs or approves on their own — deliberately NOT steps here.
roadmap.paradigm_note: The Hypothesis + state-delta unit mandate from nw-roadmap does not apply here and its omission is deliberate, not an oversight. This repository is C# + NUnit 4.6 + Moq (backend) and TypeScript + Vitest + RTL / Playwright (frontend, E2E); there is no pytest-bdd, no .feature file and no Hypothesis. DISTILL recorded it (feature-delta.md, DISTILL / Reconciliation and the mandate-compliance note under Upstream findings): layer 3+ acceptance, example-only, the one finite axis (how an earlier release left the fill) expressed as an NUnit [TestCase] over an enum. The crafter authors NO new acceptance tests in this story — the ten Story6083 cases and the three seeder unit tests were written by DISTILL and sit [Ignore]d. The crafter's RED phase is un-ignoring them and watching them fail exactly as red-classification.md recorded; its GREEN phase is production code. The only existing tests the crafter edits or deletes are the ones DISTILL's Existing-test disposition table lists, each in the same commit as the production change that makes it wrong, so no commit is red.

validation.notes: Built from feature-delta.md (DISCUSS Locked Decisions D1-D6, DISTILL Scenario list, Existing-test disposition, E2E impact, Upstream findings 1-5, Pre-requisites) and red-classification.md (11/11 MISSING_FUNCTIONALITY plus the D8 addendum). Checked against the code: (1) Scenario 11 (Clearing_the_database_leaves_the_history_fill_switched_on_like_a_new_instance) needs nothing restore-specific — the provider stand-in deletes the database and DatabaseManagementService.ClearDatabase re-migrates and re-runs every seeder, which after 01-01 seeds the fill on and writes the record. It therefore goes green in 01-01, not 01-02; it is un-ignored there and stays in 01-02 as the guard that the restore mechanism does not leak into the clear path. (2) Scenario 10 is still RED after 01-01: the restored database holds the fill off and no record, so the 01-01 seeder flips it on. That is 01-02's genuine RED. (3) DatabaseManagementService.MigrateAndSeedDatabase is shared by RestoreBackup and ClearDatabase and swallows every exception into a log line, so a record insert that collides with one already in the backup would silently abort seeding — 01-02 must insert only when absent. (4) OverTimeReconstructionSeamArchUnitTest confines the spellings OverTimeHistoryFillKey and "OverTimeHistoryFill" to OptionalFeatureKeys.cs, OptionalFeatureSeeder.cs and the switch; the record key HistoryFillSwitchedOnByDefault deliberately uses neither, so DatabaseManagementService may name the record without widening that allow-list. (5) The E2E cleanup hooks in PbcOverTime/PercentilesOverTime/PredictabilityOverTime.spec.ts carry no comment; the two comments that call off 'the shipped default' are the switchHistoryFill doc comment in tests/helpers/api/optionalFeatures.ts and the testWithDemoHistoryFill comment in Screenshots.spec.ts (~line 725). (6) Lighthouse.EndToEndTests has `tsc` (script `build`) and Biome 2.5.14 as devDependencies; its `prebuild` runs `biome check --write`, so 01-03 uses the read-only forms `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm exec biome check ./tests`. (7) The seeder's OverTimeHistoryFill description contains no 'off by default' wording, so AC-1.5's description clause needs no edit and SeedAsync_OverTimeHistoryFill_ReadsTheWayAnAdministratorSeesIt stays as it is.

user_decisions: D1 — every existing instance gets the fill on, once, on the first start-up of this release, whether its off was seeded or chosen; an admin's off after that is honoured. The release notes say so plainly.
D2 — new instances are seeded on.

D3 — 'once' is recorded by an AppSettings row the seeder writes (AppSettingKeys.HistoryFillSwitchedOnByDefault), not by an EF migration and not in AppSettingSeeder's defaults list. No schema change, no CreateMigration run.
D4 — it stays a Preview (IsPreview = true, IsPremium = false).
D5 — loading demo data neither switches it on nor off.
D6 — user-facing text uses the configurable terms (Team, Portfolio, Work Item) and the chart names as they appear.
D7 (taken autonomously at DISTILL, maintainer to confirm before finalize) — a fill row deleted by hand after the record exists comes back on, the way a new instance gets it.

D8 (taken autonomously at DISTILL, maintainer to confirm before finalize) — a restore never flips: the fill comes back as the backup held it and the record is written so a later restart does not flip it either. Clearing the database is a new instance: seeded on, record written.
out_of_scope: Telling a deliberate off apart from a seeded off, retroactively or by recording toggles from now on (D1).
Removing the switch or the Preview badge (#6084).
Any change to how the fill works: its bounds, budget, maintenance gate, the reconciler or the filler.
A start-up warning or in-app notice that the switch flipped. The release notes carry that message.
Any frontend production change. BehaviourSettingsTable renders whatever the endpoint returns.
The two-replicas-upgrading-at-once race (Upstream finding 5): pre-existing class of risk, not scenario'd.

steps.name: A restore brings the fill back as the backup held it
steps.description: After DatabaseManagementService.RestoreBackup puts a backup in place and re-runs migrations and every seeder, the fill keeps the Enabled value the backup held, the HistoryFillSwitchedOnByDefault record is present, and a later restart does not flip it either. ClearDatabase keeps behaving as a fresh install (seeded on, record written), and application start-up keeps flipping. The mechanism is the crafter's choice; prefer the smallest. Candidate A (recommended): the restore path — and only the restore path — inserts the record, if absent, after ApplyMigrations and before SeedDatabase, so the seeder sees an already-settled instance and never flips; e.g. MigrateAndSeedDatabase takes a flag that RestoreBackup sets and ClearDatabase does not, or RestoreBackup calls a small private step. Touches DatabaseManagementService.cs only, names the record key but not the fill's key, so the ArchUnit seam allow-list is untouched. Candidate B: an explicit 'after restore' signal the seeder reads (an overload of DatabaseConfigurator.SeedDatabase or a scoped occasion object) — touches DatabaseConfigurator.cs and OptionalFeatureSeeder.cs and probably a DI registration in Program.cs, which forces the full Integration suite; choose it only if A proves unworkable, and say why in the commit body. Un-ignore scenario 10.
